incumbent_reading: The paper uses the forensic biology unit as the benchmark: statistical conventions, review and reviewable outputs make a messy, judgment-heavy process look objective to outsiders (C14), and that standing is what the other units are compared against (C02).

wager.statement:
Retold from the forensic biology unit's own fragments, the paper's episode has no event in it. None of the unit's fourteen fragments has a DNA analyst speak of the 2009 report, of being the standard, or of the other units; the nearest is the supervisors introducing themselves, as a joke, on the author's first day, as the 'DNA princesses' (F28). What the fragments do carry is the unit's account of its own work and one line of history.

At the bench the analysts regard profiling as judgment-laden and untidy, because instrument output can contain artifacts and samples can be dirty, degraded or contaminated (F48). Terri describes a contaminated saliva control that cleared when she repeated the amplification, and Carly says contamination can persist with no identifiable cause (F49). In the paper's description, conclusions often took repeated interpretation and discussion between analyst and reviewer, sometimes with others brought in (F50), and Terri remarks that writing a report could take the wider laboratory (F51). What goes out is a profile released after technical and administrative review (F45) and a report that pairs a contributor conclusion with a population-frequency figure (F46). And the method became established over roughly twenty-five years, after technical advances, court challenges and favorable National Academy assessments in the 1990s (F43, which the paper draws from cited sources).

The wager from this side: the forensic biology unit is not the fixed point the other three are measured from but one more unit whose work is judgment talked through with a reviewer, and whose occupation was itself under court challenge and Academy assessment first. The firearms review in F69, two examiners debating how much agreement is enough, is the nearest printed counterpart to F50. Review of an analyst's work by someone else is printed for every unit (F45 with F50, F68, F92, F110); what is printed for forensic biology alone is the population-frequency figure (F46). If so, what each neighbor is compared with (C13) and found compatible or incompatible with (C04; F145, F146, F147, author's account) is what leaves the DNA unit, and the judgment that the paper's table sets against the objectivity associated with DNA (F148, author's account) is present on the DNA side as well (F48).

This agrees with the paper on the substance of C14, untidy work and outputs that look objective, and uses the same fragments. It differs in where it puts the unit: among the cases, with a history of being evaluated, and not above them. Whether the review steps and the figure are what that earlier evaluation left behind is not printed, and the reading does not assert it.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: What the forensic biology analysts said or did about being the standard, to the other units, to legal audiences, or about the report that exempted their work; and whether the review steps and the frequency figure were in place before the court challenges and assessments that F43 records or were taken on in their course.
what_it_would_take_to_cohere.basis: Not in the record. Of the unit's fourteen fragments (F07, F09, F13, F17, F21, F28, F43, F45, F46, F47, F48, F49, F50, F51) only F28 has DNA staff refer to themselves as a group, and it is a joke on the author's first day. F43 gives the sequence of advances, challenges and assessments without saying what the occupation or the unit changed along the way. F36 has management instruct staff to read the report and prints no reaction from this unit. F54 and F55 print what others say about DNA's resources, not what the DNA unit says back.

strains_against: F60 -- the report states that techniques such as toolmark comparison had produced some erroneous results when compared with DNA evidence in the same cases; there DNA evidence is what the others are found wrong against, a standing above the other cases that the analysts' view of their own bench work (F48) does not remove.

F49 -- the incident involves a control sample and an amplification that was repeated, after which the problem was gone; the judgment here is exercised over a step that can be run again, and no counterpart to that is printed in the firearms review of F69, so the two kinds of work may be less alike than the reading needs.

F46 -- the population-frequency calculation is a step of the work as well as a feature of the report, as is assigning alleles across sixteen loci in F45; the line between the bench and what leaves the unit is the reading's, and these two stubs sit across it.

F86 -- the MCCL firearms examiners held that a DNA-like statistical population made little sense for firearm marks; they treat the figure as something their evidence cannot have, which makes the difference one of the evidence and not only of what is handed outward.
F43 -- the same stub lists technical advances and favorable assessments; the standing may have been earned by the technique, as the paper's account has it, with nothing left behind by the challenges.
F28 -- a joke on a first day may carry no view of the unit's standing; the stub prints no explanation, and the reading cannot lean on it.
wager.who_could_complete_it: Analysts and supervisors of the forensic biology unit speaking about the comparison; the unit's own procedural history, meaning when its review steps and its statistical reporting were introduced.

grounded_in.question: Did the forensic biology analysts, anywhere in print, speak about being the standard, either putting it forward before neighbors or legal audiences or disowning it?
grounded_in.if_one_way: If they are printed putting it forward, C13 would read with the benchmark partly kept up by the benchmark unit itself, and the features the neighbors select would be features DNA analysts advance.
grounded_in.if_the_other: If they are printed disowning it, as F48 leans, C13 would read with the neighbors selecting features of what leaves the DNA unit that its own analysts do not claim for the work.

grounded_in.question: Were the technical and administrative review (F45) and the population-frequency figure (F46) in place before the court challenges and Academy assessments of F43, or adopted in their course?
grounded_in.if_one_way: If in place before, C02 would read as stated: a technique whose own features carried it to benchmark standing, after which evaluation turned on the neighbors.
grounded_in.if_the_other: If adopted in their course, C02 would read with DNA as an earlier recipient of the same evaluation, and the benchmark as what that evaluation left in one occupation's practice.

grounded_in.how: F48 has the DNA analysts regard their own profiling as judgment-laden and untidy; F148, in the author's voice, sets the objectivity associated with DNA against firearms' commitment to trained subjective judgment. The first puts judgment inside DNA work; the second places DNA across the line from judgment. The paper marks the same gap itself at F52; the reading uses it against the table's compatibility cells and not only under C14.

rival: The paper's own placing of the unit: C14 already says DNA work is messy and its outputs look objective, and C13 already says neighbors take up selected features. On that reading the unit's history (F43) is background and its bench talk is the point C14 makes; putting the unit among the cases adds nothing, because what bears on the neighbors is how courts, media and the public treat DNA (F52, author's account), whatever DNA analysts think of their own work.

verdicts.note: CLEAR. The factual clauses in the statement and fragment_jobs have carrying fragments. The card has no separating feature to assess because split is null. Its proposed placement of DNA among the cases and its interpretation of the comparison as directed at outgoing evidence are arguments from the printed material, not reports of additional events, motives, or historical changes. In particular, it expressly withholds the causal claim that earlier evaluation produced the review procedures or frequency calculation. No imported factual assertion was identified. No author-to-participant drift was identified: the card distinguishes the author's accounts from analysts' speech and from the paper's workflow descriptions.

considered_not_fired.item: The fourteen-fragment count and the assertion that none prints a DNA analyst speaking about the 2009 report, benchmark standing, or the other units.
considered_not_fired.why: The corpus assigns exactly F07, F09, F13, F17, F21, F28, F43, F45, F46, F47, F48, F49, F50, and F51 to forensic biology. Inspection supports the bounded absence claim. F07 describes size, work, and CODIS; F09, F13, F17, and F21 are descriptive table cells. F28 prints the supervisors' first-day joke, without explaining its meaning. F51 concerns help with report writing, not a statement about the unit's comparative standing. The claim is about what is printed, not proof that analysts never discussed these matters.

considered_not_fired.item: The connective 'because' in the account of judgment-laden, untidy profiling, and the contamination example.
considered_not_fired.why: F48 itself connects the analysts' view to instrument artifacts and dirty, degraded, or contaminated samples. F49 carries Terri's saliva-control problem, its disappearance after repeated amplification, and Carly's statement about persistent unexplained contamination. The card adds no cause for the contamination or explanation for why repetition worked.

considered_not_fired.item: Repeated interpretation, analyst-reviewer discussion, wider laboratory participation, and the outgoing profile and report.
considered_not_fired.why: F50 carries repeated interpretation and discussion with a reviewer, sometimes involving additional members. F51 carries Terri's remark about wider participation in report writing. F45 carries profile assembly and technical and administrative review before release. F46 carries the contributor conclusion paired with population frequency. These are paraphrases of the stubs.

considered_not_fired.item: The occupation's earlier history of evaluation and the suggestion that present procedures might be its residue.
considered_not_fired.why: F43 carries the roughly twenty-five-year establishment of forensic DNA profiling after technical advances, court challenges, and favorable Academy assessments in the 1990s; its notes identify cited historical sources. Calling this a history of being evaluated does not invent a local MCCL event. The card explicitly says that whether review and statistical reporting resulted from those evaluations is unprinted and unasserted.

considered_not_fired.item: Review by someone else in every unit and the F50-F69 comparison.
considered_not_fired.why: F45 and F50 carry DNA review; F68 carries second-examiner firearms review; F92 carries toxicology technical and supervisory review; F110 carries narcotics supervisory report review and two different crystal tests. F69 carries two examiners debating sufficient agreement. Calling F69 the nearest counterpart is the card's comparison, not a claim that all review procedures or evidential problems are identical. F110 is not made to say that a second analyst performed the second test.

considered_not_fired.item: The population-frequency figure as a feature printed for DNA alone.
considered_not_fired.why: F46 prints that particular type of figure. The other numerical practices in the corpus, including firearms CMS thresholds in F171 and toxicology confidence and uncertainty estimates in F101-F103, are not population-frequency estimates for contributor attribution. The card does not need the broader, unsupported proposition that only DNA uses numbers or statistics.

considered_not_fired.item: The 'If so' inference that the neighbors are compared with what leaves the DNA unit.
considered_not_fired.why: The outward-facing evidence has a printed basis in F45-F47 and the author's account of outside reception in F52. F85 prints firearms examiners' concern with numerical conclusions, and F122 prints concern about persistent output for later review in narcotics. F145-F148 supply the table characterizations the card explicitly reinterprets. The sentence proposes an interpretation of these comparisons; it does not introduce an unprinted act of comparison by a DNA analyst or assert that shared review caused benchmark standing.

considered_not_fired.item: Attribution of the objectivity account and the table's compatibility judgments.
considered_not_fired.why: The jobs for F47 and F52 identify the author's account, and the statement explicitly labels F145-F148 as the author's account. F48 independently carries the analysts' view that DNA work involves judgment. Agreeing with C14 and contrasting that view with the table does not put the author's explanation into an analyst's mouth.

considered_not_fired.item: The remaining jobs concerning management, resource complaints, and declared strains.
considered_not_fired.why: F36 carries management's distribution and reading instruction without a DNA-unit reaction; F54 carries non-DNA members' resource complaints; F55 carries trace examiners' association and flyer. F60 carries the NAS comparison of erroneous results with DNA evidence, and F86 carries the firearms examiners' objection to a DNA-like statistical population. The card does not invent a DNA response to these statements and explicitly treats the last two as strains.

verdicts.note: CLEAR. All 172 fragments were scanned, with the eight seeds and the two additional declared-strain fragments, F60 and F86, excluded as kill grounds. No remaining stub requires an event, utterance, or practice to have been different for this focalization to hold. The claim of 'no event' is bounded by the following sentence to the absence of a printed DNA-unit response to the report or comparison; it does not deny the report's occurrence or the unit's everyday incidents. The proposed relocation of DNA within the analysis does not erase its documented external privilege. Disagreement with the author's benchmark and compatibility account is not a contradiction of an event. The absence register and fragment notes were also checked.

considered_not_fired.item: F01, F32, F36, and F44: DNA's exemption, the report's circulation, and published advocacy of DNA as a model.
considered_not_fired.why: These are real printed acts of external evaluation or management communication. They do not print a DNA analyst's reaction. The card expressly asks about the report that exempted DNA and acknowledges benchmark treatment, so placing the unit among historically evaluated occupations does not require denying these acts.

considered_not_fired.item: F52, F54, and F55: external benchmark treatment and resource privilege.
considered_not_fired.why: F52 is explicitly the author's account, which the card acknowledges. F54 and F55 print other groups' complaints and organizational activity. Those events can coexist with DNA analysts describing judgment-heavy work and with no printed DNA reply. They do not establish that the unit itself asserted or disowned benchmark standing.

considered_not_fired.item: F145-F148 and the broader benchmark interpretations in F39-F42 and F154-F158.
considered_not_fired.why: The relevant statements characterize the author's explanation of comparison, compatibility, and occupational interpretation. The card identifies this account and proposes another focal position. Disagreement with those characterizations cannot by itself fire E; the card does not deny that the table or explanation was printed.

considered_not_fired.item: F82 and F85: firearms examiners rejecting equivalence to DNA and discussing statistics and objectivity.
considered_not_fired.why: Shared review and judgment do not entail interchangeable techniques, equal numerical resources, or agreement among examiners that firearms resembles DNA. F85's focus on numerical conclusions is also compatible with the proposed attention to outgoing evidence. The related objection to a statistical population is explicitly declared at F86.

considered_not_fired.item: F67-F69, F92, F110, and F124: distinct review and documentation practices.
considered_not_fired.why: The card claims that review by another person is printed for all units, not that every unit repeats the same analysis or preserves the same evidence. In particular, F124's contemplated independent visual confirmation of crystals is compatible with F110's existing supervisory review of reports and two-test requirement. The proposal need not already have been implemented for the card's review comparison to hold.

considered_not_fired.item: F98 and F101-F103, together with F171: statistics and numerical rules outside DNA.
considered_not_fired.why: Toxicology's existing and expanded uncertainty reporting and firearms' numerical matching thresholds do not contradict the narrower statement that a contributor population-frequency figure is printed for DNA alone. The reading also does not assert that the NAS report initiated every reporting change; F98 and F102 can stand as printed.

considered_not_fired.item: F122, F125, F127, and F128: narcotics analysts' concerns about retained output, equipment, training, and monotonous instrument work.
considered_not_fired.why: F122 and F125 connect the debate to preserving reviewable evidence. F127 and F128 show that changing the method would also affect expertise and work variety. Those consequences can coexist with an outward-facing comparison standard: the card does not assert that changing outputs leaves work unchanged, or that shared judgment eliminates occupational values and technique differences.

considered_not_fired.item: F60, F86, and the remaining declared strains and seeds.
considered_not_fired.why: DNA evidence as a check on erroneous findings in F60 and the evidence-specific statistical difficulty in F86 are substantial pressure on the reading, but both are declared strains. F28, F43, F46, and F49 are also declared strains and seeds; F45, F48, F50, and F51 are the other seeds. None is eligible to supply an undeclared-contradiction kill under E.

considered_not_fired.item: Missing DNA responses and procedural history; A01 and DG03.
considered_not_fired.why: The corpus supplies neither a DNA-unit response to the benchmark comparison nor a chronology linking its review and statistical reporting to earlier challenges. These omissions are identified as missing evidence in the card, not contradicted by a printed event. A01 and DG03 concern uncollected local actions of externally challenged firearms examiners; they provide no contrary DNA history and cannot supply a contradiction by inference.

attack.kept: A killed reading is retained, marked. Deleting it removes the evidence that the pass functions.
